sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In 2019, two hunters were scouting for elk in Wyoming when they came across a peculiar feature in the landscape.
sentences.zh: 2019年，两名猎人在怀俄明州寻找麋鹿时，偶然发现了一处奇特的地貌。

sentences.en: The hunters had first noticed it while poring over maps of the area.
sentences.zh: 猎人们最初是在仔细研究该地区的地图时注意到的。

sentences.en: Now they were driving out to see it for themselves, a kind of break in the terrain near the state's southeast corner.
sentences.zh: 现在他们正开车前往实地查看，那是该州东南角附近的一处地形断层。

sentences.en: So it's open country.
sentences.zh: 那是一片开阔地。

sentences.en: It's open ranch country, sagebrush country.
sentences.zh: 那是开阔的牧场，长满了山艾树。

sentences.en: And then there's this big mountain sticking up right there in the middle of it that just, it's the only mountain.
sentences.zh: 就在那片开阔地的正中央，突兀地耸立着一座大山，那是唯一的一座山。

sentences.en: Brad Cape is a fencing contractor from central Missouri.
sentences.zh: 布拉德·凯普是来自密苏里州中部的一名围栏承包商。

sentences.en: Brad has been hunting since he was old enough to walk.
sentences.zh: 布拉德从能走路起就开始打猎了。

sentences.en: So when he and his hunting partner saw the Lone Mountain with its dark timber and the arid, empty land around it, he knew what it meant.
sentences.zh: 所以当他和狩猎伙伴看到那座有着深色树木、周围荒凉空旷的“孤山”时，他明白这意味着什么。

sentences.en: It is a very unique place.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常独特的地方。

sentences.en: And you can see on a map that it's a very unique place.
sentences.zh: 从地图上也能看出那是一个非常独特的地方。

sentences.en: It is a rocky mountain that sits out by itself.
sentences.zh: 那是一座孤零零矗立着的岩石山。

sentences.en: You know, it might as well have a big bullseye on it that says there's elk here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它上面简直就像画了个大靶心，写着“这里有麋鹿”。

sentences.en: And it's true.
sentences.zh: 事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: The mountain basically screamed good hunting.
sentences.zh: 这座山简直在大声呼喊着“这里是绝佳的狩猎场”。

sentences.en: That's Montana-based journalist Nick Mott.
sentences.zh: 说话的是蒙大拿州的记者尼克·莫特。

sentences.en: I'm a hunter too, so I get how Brad felt when he found this spot.
sentences.zh: 我也是个猎人，所以我很理解布拉德发现这个地方时的心情。

sentences.en: Poring over land boundaries and topographic lines, trying to figure out where animals are and other hunters aren't.
sentences.zh: 仔细研究土地边界和地形图，试图弄清楚动物在哪里，而其他猎人又不在哪里。

sentences.en: Finding that perfect area is often nearly as exciting as the hunt itself.
sentences.zh: 找到那片完美的区域，往往和狩猎本身一样令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And this time, all the pieces of the puzzle were fitting into place.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，拼图的所有碎片都拼凑在了一起。

sentences.en: The area had everything big game needed.
sentences.zh: 该地区拥有大型猎物所需的一切。

sentences.en: Forage, water, cover.
sentences.zh: 草料、水源、掩体。

sentences.en: On the map, the peak was named Elk Mountain.
sentences.zh: 在地图上，这座山峰被命名为“麋鹿山”。

sentences.en: Which, you know, was probably another big clue.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这可能又是另一个巨大的线索。

sentences.en: And so we were driving around it.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开车绕着它转。

sentences.en: We were just seeing how close we could get to this mountain.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想看看能离这座山有多近。

sentences.en: And this sweet old gal pulls up there and rolls down her window and asks if she can help us, you know.
sentences.zh: 这时，一位和蔼的老太太开车过来，摇下车窗问我们是否需要帮助。

sentences.en: And we said, well, we're just looking for a way to that mountain.
sentences.zh: 我们说，哦，我们只是在找去那座山的路。

sentences.en: Is there a way to get up there?
sentences.zh: 有路能上去吗？

sentences.en: We'd like to, we're thinking about hunting it.
sentences.zh: 我们想上去，我们在考虑去那里打猎。

sentences.en: And she's like, there's no way up there.
sentences.zh: 她说，没路上去。

sentences.en: A billionaire bought it and he don't let nobody in.
sentences.zh: 一个亿万富翁把它买下了，他不让任何人进去。

sentences.en: And we said, oh, okay, you know, well, is there, is there any elk around here or deer around here?
sentences.zh: 我们说，哦，好吧，那这附近有麋鹿或鹿吗？

sentences.en: That's when this sweet old gal told them there were so many elk in the area, they'd actually become a nuisance.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，那位和蔼的老太太告诉他们，该地区的麋鹿多到已经成了困扰。

sentences.en: Eating the hay meant for cattle.
sentences.zh: 它们在吃本该喂牛的干草。

sentences.en: And we just kind of looked at each other and said, yes, ma'am, thank you for your time, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们互相看了看，说，好的，女士，谢谢您的时间。

sentences.en: And we were excited from that moment on that we were going to find a way in there.
sentences.zh: 从那一刻起，我们就很兴奋，一定要找到进去的路。

sentences.en: But finding a way in there wasn't going to be easy.
sentences.zh: 但要找到进去的路并不容易。

sentences.en: Brad and his fellow hunters would end up trying to access Elk Mountain again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 布拉德和他的同伴们最终一次又一次地尝试进入麋鹿山。

sentences.en: Until, eventually, it wasn't even about hunting elk anymore, but something way bigger than that.
sentences.zh: 直到最后，这甚至不再仅仅是为了猎鹿，而是关乎更重大的事情。

sentences.en: And whether they succeeded or not would end up having lasting consequences for the future of land use everywhere in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们是否成功，最终将对美国各地土地使用的未来产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: Because the single largest obstacle preventing the hunters from making it onto Elk Mountain wasn't the elevation or the topography.
sentences.zh: 因为阻碍猎人们进入麋鹿山的最大障碍，并不是海拔或地形。

sentences.en: It was how the mountain itself had been divided up into public and private land.
sentences.zh: 而是这座山本身是如何被划分为公共土地和私人土地的。

sentences.en: When you look at that place on a map, it looks like a bunch of these little bitty squares.
sentences.zh: 当你从地图上看那个地方时，它看起来像是一堆小方块。

sentences.en: And when you start looking at it, you see that it is, it's a checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 当你开始仔细观察时，你会发现它确实是一个棋盘。

sentences.en: The checkerboard, as it's commonly known, is a phenomenon unique to the American WeSt.
sentences.zh: 这种“棋盘格”是美国西部特有的现象。

sentences.en: A pattern of land ownership, which is found in huge areas from New Mexico all the way up to Washington.
sentences.zh: 这是一种土地所有权模式，从新墨西哥州一直延伸到华盛顿州，覆盖了广阔的区域。

sentences.en: On a map, these particular areas look a lot like, well, a checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 在地图上，这些特定的区域看起来很像棋盘。

sentences.en: Or perhaps checkered linoleum tiles.
sentences.zh: 或者说是方格油毡地砖。

sentences.en: But instead of alternating black and white squares, checkerboarded land alternates between single square mile parcels of public land and square mile parcels of private land.
sentences.zh: 但不同于黑白交替的方格，棋盘格土地是在一平方英里的公共土地和一平方英里的私人土地之间交替。

sentences.en: So every public square borders a private square.
sentences.zh: 所以每一个公共方格都与一个私人方格相邻。

sentences.en: Which borders a public square?
sentences.zh: 而它又与一个公共方格相邻？

sentences.en: Which borders a private square?
sentences.zh: 又与一个私人方格相邻？

sentences.en: Which borders a public square?
sentences.zh: 又与一个公共方格相邻？

sentences.en: Which borders a...
sentences.zh: 又与一个……

sentences.en: Well, you get the idea.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你明白我的意思了。

sentences.en: If you look out of an airplane window while flying over a checkerboarded area,
sentences.zh: 如果你在飞越棋盘格区域时从飞机窗户往下看，

sentences.en: it's not uncommon to see one square with a private housing development on it while the next sits relatively untouched.
sentences.zh: 经常会看到一个方格上有私人住宅开发项目，而隔壁的方格却相对未受破坏。

sentences.en: Or perhaps every other square features dense forest on public land while those private squares in between are logged.
sentences.zh: 或者，每隔一个方格就是公共土地上的茂密森林，而中间的私人方格却被砍伐了。

sentences.en: Again, just think of those alternating tiles.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，想想那些交替的地砖。

sentences.en: An image which Brad finds himself invoking all the time.
sentences.zh: 布拉德发现自己总是会用到这个比喻。

sentences.en: Still, to this day, if I have someone ask me about this in the grocery store, I can't explain it.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，如果有人在杂货店问我这件事，我都解释不清楚。

sentences.en: Unless I'm standing on a tile floor.
sentences.zh: 除非我正站在铺着地砖的地面上。

sentences.en: Because here in the Midwest and the rest of the country, they just don't get it.
sentences.zh: 因为在中西部和全国其他地方，他们根本不理解这一点。

sentences.en: There's a catch, though, when it comes to hunting or doing anything, really, on the checkerboarded area.
sentences.zh: 不过，在棋盘格区域打猎或做任何事情，确实有一个陷阱。

sentences.en: In the U.S., there's no legal way to pass through private property without the landowner's permission.
sentences.zh: 在美国，未经土地所有者许可，没有合法途径可以穿过私人领地。

sentences.en: That's trespassing.
sentences.zh: 那是擅闯民宅。

sentences.en: So public land in the checkerboard is often very difficult to access.
sentences.zh: 所以棋盘格中的公共土地通常很难进入。

sentences.en: After all, any public square in a checkerboard is surrounded on all sides by private property.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，棋盘格中的任何公共方格四周都被私人领地包围着。

sentences.en: It's only ever catty-corner to other public squares.
sentences.zh: 它只能在对角线上与其他公共方格相连。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter that the public land belongs to us, the public.
sentences.zh: 公共土地属于我们公众，这一点并不重要。

sentences.en: The reality is, it's only the owners of the adjacent private squares who have an easy way in.
sentences.zh: 现实是，只有相邻私人方格的所有者才有便捷的进入途径。

sentences.en: These inaccessible public lands are what's called corner-locked.
sentences.zh: 这些无法进入的公共土地被称为“角锁”土地。

sentences.en: So it's a big deal out west because you have the layout of public land out there,
sentences.zh: 这在西部是个大问题，因为那里有公共土地的布局，

sentences.en: but you're just trying to keep the access to yourself.
sentences.zh: 但你却试图把通道据为己有。

sentences.en: And when it came to hunting in the checkerboard on Elk Mountain, it was no different.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到在麋鹿山的棋盘格上打猎时，情况也没什么不同。

sentences.en: The private half of the checkerboard belonged to a ranch.
sentences.zh: 棋盘格的私人部分属于一个牧场。

sentences.en: And the ranch wasn't allowing strangers to cross their land.
sentences.zh: 而牧场不允许陌生人穿过他们的土地。

sentences.en: But to Brad, that just made the public land all the more tantalizing.
sentences.zh: 但对布拉德来说，这反而让公共土地变得更加诱人。

sentences.en: Because it meant that it had the one thing that any good hunter was looking for.
sentences.zh: 因为它意味着那里有任何优秀猎人都在寻找的东西。

sentences.en: No other hunters.
sentences.zh: 没有其他猎人。

sentences.en: So the next year, in 2020, Brad and his friends,
sentences.zh: 所以第二年，也就是2020年，布拉德和他的朋友们，

sentences.en: they decided to try something that, in hunting circles, is called corner crossing.
sentences.zh: 他们决定尝试一种在狩猎圈子里被称为“对角跨越”的方法。

sentences.en: Because something where nobody else would be, that's where I want to be.
sentences.zh: 因为没人会去的地方，那才是我想要去的地方。

sentences.en: And in order to do that, we had to cross these corners.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我们必须跨越这些角落。

sentences.en: To understand corner crossing, think about a literal checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 要理解“对角跨越”，可以想象一个真正的棋盘。

sentences.en: In a checkers game, a piece that starts on black needs to stay on black.
sentences.zh: 在跳棋游戏中，从黑色方格开始的棋子需要保持在黑色方格上。

sentences.en: So the pieces move diagonally, crossing catty corner from the corner of one square to another.
sentences.zh: 所以棋子是斜着移动的，从一个方格的角落跨越到另一个方格的角落。

sentences.en: Moving through checkerboarded land works in the same way.
sentences.zh: 在棋盘格土地上移动也是同样的道理。

sentences.en: To avoid the ranch's property, all Brad and his friends had to do was move around like a checkers piece.
sentences.zh: 为了避开牧场的领地，布拉德和他的朋友们所要做的就是像跳棋棋子一样移动。

sentences.en: They'd start on public land and then make sure to stay on public land
sentences.zh: 他们从公共土地出发，然后确保一直待在公共土地上，

sentences.en: by only crossing into new squares diagonally, at the corners where all those public squares touch.
sentences.zh: 只在所有公共方格相交的角落处，斜向跨入新的方格。

sentences.en: Tell me about, you know, you, I mean, so the way it works in this area, like, you set up camp
sentences.zh: 跟我说说，你是怎么做的，我的意思是，在这个区域，你是这样操作的：你先扎营，

sentences.en: and your camp is in the first, like, square that is publicly accessible and then you cross from there.
sentences.zh: 你的营地在第一个公共可进入的方格里，然后你从那里跨越。

sentences.en: Like, how did that work?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly what it was.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那样。

sentences.en: That's Phil Yeomans.
sentences.zh: 那是菲尔·约曼斯。

sentences.en: Phil is also from Missouri and he's been hunting with Brad for about a decade.
sentences.zh: 菲尔也来自密苏里州，他和布拉德一起打猎大约十年了。

sentences.en: Phil explained that, this time, they all hiked from a public road towards the checkerboard's nearest approachable corner.
sentences.zh: 菲尔解释说，这一次，他们都从一条公共道路徒步走向棋盘格最近的可接近角落。

sentences.en: When they got there, in the middle of this empty field,
sentences.zh: 当他们到达那里时，在这片空旷的田野中央，

sentences.en: there was a little government survey marker about the size of a Coke can.
sentences.zh: 有一个大约可乐罐大小的小型政府测量标记。

sentences.en: There were also two no-trespassing signs, along with a couple of posts called T-posts with a chain strung between them.
sentences.zh: 还有两个“禁止擅入”的标志，以及几根被称为T型柱的柱子，中间拉着一条链子。

sentences.en: Which was ironic, considering it was obstructing the one spot where they could legally cross.
sentences.zh: 这很讽刺，因为它正好挡住了他们可以合法跨越的唯一地点。

sentences.en: So, um, we just grabbed hold of the top of that T-post and swung our feet around, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，我们只是抓住那根T型柱的顶部，把脚甩过去，你知道，

sentences.en: kind of doing a little ballerina around the T-post so that we didn't touch the private property.
sentences.zh: 就像绕着T型柱跳了一段小芭蕾，这样我们就不会碰到私人领地。

sentences.en: Yeah, we weren't, we weren't nonchalant about it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们并不是漫不经心。

sentences.en: We were very specific, you know, as in we planted our foot exactly.
sentences.zh: 我们非常谨慎，你知道，我们精确地落脚。

sentences.en: From that point on, they made sure to stay entirely on public land their whole time inside the checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他们确保在棋盘格内的整个时间都完全待在公共土地上。

sentences.en: They corner-crossed from one public square to another as they hunted for elk on Elk Mountain.
sentences.zh: 他们在麋鹿山上猎鹿时，从一个公共方格对角跨越到另一个公共方格。

sentences.en: And from the start, the mountain proved true to its name.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，这座山就名副其实。

sentences.en: Man, that first morning, the bulls were bugling.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那个清晨，公麋鹿在鸣叫。

sentences.en: We could hear them from the county road.
sentences.zh: 我们在县道上就能听到它们的声音。

sentences.en: And, uh, once we got up to the place, we decided we were going to camp.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，一旦我们到达那个地方，我们决定扎营。

sentences.en: We saw a big old herd coming, walking down the side hill.
sentences.zh: 我们看到一大群麋鹿走下山坡。

sentences.en: And we just stood there and watched them.
sentences.zh: 我们只是站在那里看着它们。

sentences.en: It was like, this is going to be good.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉是，这会很棒。

sentences.en: But we were up the mountain, up the mountain, up the mountain.
sentences.zh: 但我们一直在爬山，爬山，爬山。

sentences.en: And we ended up so far up that mountain, we drank water out of an elk track seeping out of the hill that day.
sentences.zh: 我们最终爬得太高了，那天我们喝了从山坡渗出的麋鹿足迹里的水。

sentences.en: And this elk's bugling just as far away as you can hear, you know.
sentences.zh: 那只麋鹿的鸣叫声远到你所能听到的极限，你知道。

sentences.en: They would go on to harvest three big bull elk.
sentences.zh: 他们最终猎获了三头大公麋鹿。

sentences.en: And I can tell you, this is a big deal.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，这可是一件大事。

sentences.en: Most elk hunts lead to nothing, mine included.
sentences.zh: 大多数麋鹿狩猎都一无所获，包括我自己的。

sentences.en: And these guys got a haul.
sentences.zh: 而这些人收获颇丰。

sentences.en: But things weren't all sunshine and roses and big bugling bulls.
sentences.zh: 但事情并非全是阳光、玫瑰和大声鸣叫的公麋鹿。

sentences.en: Because just as they were field dressing a bull elk, a man appeared in the distance.
sentences.zh: 因为就在他们处理公麋鹿时，远处出现了一个人。

sentences.en: And he makes the walk over to us, which took quite a while.
sentences.zh: 他朝我们走过来，这花了不少时间。

sentences.en: We just kept work, you know, because they're half a mile, you know, from us.
sentences.zh: 我们只是继续干活，你知道，因为他们离我们有半英里远。

sentences.en: As the man walked over, Brad's friend Zach thought something felt wrong and started recording on his phone.
sentences.zh: 当那个人走过来时，布拉德的朋友扎克觉得有些不对劲，开始用手机录像。

sentences.en: So he just walks up to us and asks us what we're doing there, you know, and was a little snotty about it.
sentences.zh: 他走过来问我们在那儿干什么，你知道，态度还有点刻薄。

sentences.en: Hey, how are we doing?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你们好吗？

sentences.en: Good, how are you?
sentences.zh: 很好，你呢？

sentences.en: Worn out.
sentences.zh: 累坏了。

sentences.en: Yeah?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: How'd you get in here?
sentences.zh: 你们是怎么进来的？

sentences.en: It was the ranch's manager, a man named Steve Grindy.
sentences.zh: 那是牧场的经理，一个叫史蒂夫·格林迪的人。

sentences.en: The hunters told Grindy they got here by crossing from a public section of land to another public section at a corner.
sentences.zh: 猎人们告诉格林迪，他们是通过从一块公共土地跨越到另一个公共土地的角落进来的。

sentences.en: So on that first corner with the signs on it, how'd you get through that?
sentences.zh: 那么在那个有标志的第一个角落，你们是怎么穿过去的？

sentences.en: Grabbed the T-posts while we were at it.
sentences.zh: 我们顺便抓住了T型柱。

sentences.en: Got a chain on it so you can't go between them.
sentences.zh: 上面有链子，所以你没法从中间穿过。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But it's also on private property.
sentences.zh: 但那也是私人领地。

sentences.en: Anytime you touch that thing, it's criminal trespassing.
sentences.zh: 任何时候你触碰那个东西，都是刑事擅闯。

sentences.en: That's why they're there.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们在那里的原因。

sentences.en: But the hunters had done their research.
sentences.zh: 但猎人们做过调查。

sentences.en: They pointed out that Wyoming Fish and Game, and even the state attorney general, had said that crossing at corners was legal.
sentences.zh: 他们指出，怀俄明州鱼类和狩猎管理局，甚至州总检察长，都曾表示在角落处跨越是合法的。

sentences.en: But Grindy countered.
sentences.zh: 但格林迪反驳道。

sentences.en: You can't corner jump in Carvin County.
sentences.zh: 在卡文县，你不能进行对角跨越。

sentences.en: Period.
sentences.zh: 没门。

sentences.en: I believe everything we read says we can.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们读到的每一条信息都说我们可以这样做。

sentences.en: Well, we're just going to have to go to the court and have them decide.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们只能去法院，让他们来裁决。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: As uncomfortable as the encounter was, it wasn't out of the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 尽管那次遭遇很不愉快，但这并不罕见。

sentences.en: Spats over corner crossings happen between hunters and landowners all the time.
sentences.zh: 猎人和土地所有者之间关于“角落穿越”的争执时有发生。

sentences.en: Ultimately, it's all part of a much larger war over public and private land and the checkerboard that began over a century and a half earlier.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这都是一场关于公共土地与私人土地、以及一个半多世纪前就开始形成的“棋盘式”土地格局的更大战争的一部分。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国。

sentences.en: government has been in the business of dividing up government-owned land into squares since 1785.
sentences.zh: 政府从1785年起就开始将政府拥有的土地划分为方块。

sentences.en: The system was the brainchild of Thomas Jefferson, who dreamed of selling all those squares to a nation of small yeoman farmers.
sentences.zh: 这个系统是托马斯·杰斐逊的构想，他梦想着把所有这些方块土地卖给一个由小自耕农组成的国家。

sentences.en: But the actual checkerboarding of the land began at the tail end of the Civil War, when policymakers in Washington wanted American settlers to move weSt.
sentences.zh: 但土地真正的“棋盘化”始于内战末期，当时华盛顿的决策者希望美国定居者向西迁移。

sentences.en: Because, as anyone who's ever played Oregon Trail knows, moving out west was hard.
sentences.zh: 因为正如任何玩过《俄勒冈之旅》的人所知，向西迁移非常艰难。

sentences.en: Beyond the 100th meridian, most settlers struggled to access the necessary supplies to get their homesteads up and running or their goods to market.
sentences.zh: 在西经100度线以西，大多数定居者难以获得维持家园运转所需的物资，也难以将产品运往市场。

sentences.en: So, in the mid-1800s, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，在19世纪中叶，美国。

sentences.en: government turned to the railroads to move those supplies for them.
sentences.zh: 政府转而求助于铁路公司，让他们代为运输这些物资。

sentences.en: Only, it turned out that the railroads also needed help.
sentences.zh: 只是，事实证明铁路公司也需要帮助。

sentences.en: The railroads are not going to build by themselves.
sentences.zh: 铁路不会自己修建起来。

sentences.en: The reason they're not going to build by themselves is there's nobody out there and no traffic.
sentences.zh: 它们不会自己修建的原因是那里没有人，也没有交通流量。

sentences.en: You don't build a railroad into the middle of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 你不会把铁路修到荒无人烟的地方。

sentences.en: This isn't field of dreams, and you just hope they'll come if you build it.
sentences.zh: 这不是《梦幻之地》，你不能指望只要修了，人们就会来。

sentences.en: Richard White is professor emeritus of history at Stanford and the author of the book Railroaded, The Transcontinentals in the Making of Modern America.
sentences.zh: 理查德·怀特是斯坦福大学历史学荣休教授，也是《铁路化：现代美国的缔造与横贯大陆铁路》一书的作者。

sentences.en: So what you're going to do is you're going to have to get aid in building the railroad.
sentences.zh: 所以你要做的是，你必须在修建铁路时获得援助。

sentences.en: The federal government says we are going to prime the pump.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府说，我们要启动这个项目。

sentences.en: White says the United States was cash-poor but land-rich.
sentences.zh: 怀特说，当时的美国是“现金贫乏但土地富足”。

sentences.en: So the government gave the railroad companies long corridors of land, up to 80 miles wide on which to build new rail lines.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府给了铁路公司长长的土地走廊，宽度可达80英里，用于修建新的铁路线。

sentences.en: The railroads could then sell or lease that land to whomever they could lure weSt.
sentences.zh: 铁路公司随后可以将这些土地出售或出租给任何他们能诱导到西部去的人。

sentences.en: But the government only granted the railroads every other square mile of land.
sentences.zh: 但政府只授予铁路公司每隔一平方英里的土地。

sentences.en: Hence, the checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 因此，就形成了棋盘格局。

sentences.en: With the checkerboard,
sentences.zh: 有了这种棋盘格局，

sentences.en: the government could keep all the undeveloped sections in between and wait for them to go up in value before turning around and selling them to more developers.
sentences.zh: 政府可以保留中间所有未开发的区域，等待它们升值，然后再转手卖给更多的开发商。

sentences.en: The new railways would also transport the soldiers needed to push Native Americans off the land the U.S.
sentences.zh: 新的铁路还将运送士兵，将美洲原住民从美国承诺给他们的土地上驱逐出去，并赶往保留地。

sentences.en: had promised them and onto reservations.
sentences.zh: 所以这成为了一种征服手段。

sentences.en: So this becomes a means of conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 一旦铁路建成，一旦印第安人的土地可以被出售来修建铁路，那么铁路就能成为征服任何残余印第安抵抗力量的工具。

sentences.en: And once it's there, once the Indian lands can be sold to build the railroads, then the railroads can become the agency for conquering any remaining Indian resistance.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个系统的运作方式。

sentences.en: So this is how the whole system works.
sentences.zh: 所以，它确实成为了殖民的代理人。

sentences.en: And in this way, it does become an agent of colonization.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，它确实成为了殖民的工具。

sentences.en: Under this system, a lot of land changed hands.
sentences.zh: 在这种制度下，大量土地易手了。

sentences.en: In all, over 130 million acres went to the railroads.
sentences.zh: 总计超过1.3亿英亩的土地流向了铁路公司。

sentences.en: And to put that in perspective, if all the federal grants to railroads were combined into one state, if you called it Railroadiana,
sentences.zh: 为了让你有个概念，如果把所有联邦给予铁路的赠地合并成一个州，如果你把它命名为“铁路州”，

sentences.en: it would be the third largest state in the United States, behind Texas and Alaska.
sentences.zh: 它将是美国第三大州，仅次于德克萨斯州和阿拉斯加州。

sentences.en: One company alone, the Northern Pacific Railroad, received an amount of land roughly the size of New England.
sentences.zh: 仅北太平洋铁路公司一家，就获得了大约相当于新英格兰地区大小的土地。

sentences.en: And almost all of it was given away in alternating one-square-mile sections.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎所有这些土地都是以交错的一平方英里地块形式赠送的。

sentences.en: So the checkerboard, on paper, this is a system that's ideal.
sentences.zh: 所以，在纸面上，这个棋盘系统是理想的。

sentences.en: What can possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 能出什么问题呢？

sentences.en: It seems to be foolproof.
sentences.zh: 看起来天衣无缝。

sentences.en: But like most systems that seem to be foolproof, they're usually designed by fools.
sentences.zh: 但像大多数看起来天衣无缝的系统一样，它们通常是由傻瓜设计的。

sentences.en: And that's what's going to happen here.
sentences.zh: 而这正是这里将要发生的事情。

sentences.en: When the railroads sold their land, it went to timber companies.
sentences.zh: 当铁路公司出售土地时，买家是木材公司。

sentences.en: It went to miners.
sentences.zh: 是矿工。

sentences.en: It went to developers.
sentences.zh: 是开发商。

sentences.en: But especially ranchers, who saw a sort of two-for-one bargain on all that checkerboarded property.
sentences.zh: 但尤其是牧场主，他们在所有这些棋盘状的土地上看到了一种“买一送一”的便宜货。

sentences.en: All you had to do was buy the private squares and then fence off all the adjacent public squares.
sentences.zh: 你所要做的就是买下私人方块，然后把所有相邻的公共方块围起来。

sentences.en: And they would effectively be yours for the keeping, too.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上也就归你所有了。

sentences.en: By the 1880s, big cattle barons had fenced in millions of acres of land they didn't own.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪80年代，大牧场主们已经圈占了数百万英亩他们并不拥有的土地。

sentences.en: But homesteaders and smaller-scale ranchers and farmers weren't happy about all that fence.
sentences.zh: 但定居者以及小规模的牧场主和农民对这些围栏并不满意。

sentences.en: The fences block settlers because settlers have to be able to drive their wagons, get to railroad depots, and they're blocked by fences.
sentences.zh: 围栏阻碍了定居者，因为定居者必须能够驾驶马车，到达铁路仓库，而他们被围栏挡住了。

sentences.en: The tension between settlers and ranchers quickly grew ugly.
sentences.zh: 定居者和牧场主之间的紧张关系很快恶化。

sentences.en: There were standoffs, shootouts, murders.
sentences.zh: 出现了对峙、枪战和谋杀。

sentences.en: Later on, dime novels, radio programs, and television shows like Gunsmoke would dramatize this era, known as the Range Wars.
sentences.zh: 后来，廉价小说、广播节目和像《荒野大镖客》这样的电视节目将这一时期戏剧化，即所谓的“牧场战争”。

sentences.en: Those cattlemen built this country, man.
sentences.zh: 伙计，是那些牧牛人建设了这个国家。

sentences.en: A few more years, now they'll have us fenced out.
sentences.zh: 再过几年，他们就会把我们挡在围栏外面了。

sentences.en: Times change, Ben.
sentences.zh: 时代变了，本。

sentences.en: In 1885, in an effort to curtail the power of the big ranchers,
sentences.zh: 1885年，为了遏制大牧场主的权力，

sentences.en: Congress finally stepped in and passed the Unlawful Enclosures Act, which guaranteed public access to public land.
sentences.zh: 国会终于介入并颁布了《非法圈地法》，保证了公众进入公共土地的权利。

sentences.en: You can still build fences around your own land.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以在自己的土地周围修建围栏。

sentences.en: You can control access if there hasn't been a right-of-way established across your own land.
sentences.zh: 如果你的土地上没有建立通行权，你可以控制进入。

sentences.en: But you cannot enclose public land.
sentences.zh: 但你不能圈占公共土地。

sentences.en: And you cannot enclose land that you do not own.
sentences.zh: 而且你不能圈占你不拥有的土地。

sentences.en: Today, the Unlawful Enclosures Act is still on the books.
sentences.zh: 今天，《非法圈地法》仍然有效。

sentences.en: But the Act never did much to break up the ranches and other big properties of the western U.S.
sentences.zh: 但该法案从未在瓦解美国西部的牧场和其他大型地产方面发挥太大作用。

sentences.en: And those large landowners never stopped looking for ways to secure their property, including in the checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 而那些大土地所有者从未停止寻找保护其财产的方法，包括在棋盘地带。

sentences.en: That part never seems to change.
sentences.zh: 那部分似乎永远不会改变。

sentences.en: So Jefferson's dream of this whole thing ending up as being small farms, that is just simply not the case.
sentences.zh: 所以杰斐逊关于这一切最终会变成小农场的梦想，根本不是那么回事。

sentences.en: The West ends up as a place of very, very large land holdings.
sentences.zh: 西部最终成为了拥有非常、非常大片土地的地方。

sentences.en: And it still very much was when Brad and the hunters stepped from corner to corner of public land in 2020.
sentences.zh: 当布拉德和猎人们在2020年从公共土地的一个角落跨越到另一个角落时，情况依然如此。

sentences.en: After that first hunting trip, they could easily have left and just never come back.
sentences.zh: 在那次狩猎旅行之后，他们本可以轻松离开，再也不回来。

sentences.en: Why risk another awkward run-in?
sentences.zh: 为什么要冒再次发生尴尬冲突的风险呢？

sentences.en: But in the end, the hunting was just too good.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，狩猎体验实在太棒了。

sentences.en: Plus, they'd spoken with law enforcement who told them they were good to go.
sentences.zh: 另外，他们咨询过执法部门，对方告诉他们可以这样做。

sentences.en: After all, the Unlawful Enclosures Act was still in force.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，《非法圈地法》仍然有效。

sentences.en: So the following year, they went back to hunt Elk Mountain.
sentences.zh: 所以第二年，他们又回到了麋鹿山狩猎。

sentences.en: But this time, just to be on the safe side, they made one small adjustment to their corner-crossing strategy.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，为了保险起见，他们对“角落穿越”策略做了一个小小的调整。

sentences.en: The only thing that we had that the ranch complained about was that we touched their T-poSt.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一被牧场投诉过的事情就是我们碰到了他们的T型柱。

sentences.en: You know, so we just had to get past that T-post without touching it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以我们只需要在不触碰T型柱的情况下越过它。

sentences.en: And then there was nothing that they could say.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就无话可说了。

sentences.en: So that's where the whole ladder idea came in.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是梯子这个主意的由来。

sentences.en: If they shouldn't touch the T-posts, then why not find a way to climb right over them?
sentences.zh: 如果他们不应该触碰T型柱，那为什么不找个办法直接爬过去呢？

sentences.en: What did you build?
sentences.zh: 你做了什么？

sentences.en: Like, how did you build the ladder?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做这个梯子的？

sentences.en: This, you know, this wouldn't be my solution necessarily.
sentences.zh: 这，你知道，这不一定是我的解决方案。

sentences.en: I wouldn't think about building a ladder.
sentences.zh: 我不会想到去造个梯子。

sentences.en: Like, what goes into it?
sentences.zh: 这需要什么准备？

sentences.en: Well, I guess maybe if you were a pole vaulter, you would take a pole vault with you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想如果你是个撑杆跳运动员，你可能会带一根撑杆。

sentences.en: I was a fence guy, you know, so I had access to a lot of pipe and a welder.
sentences.zh: 我是个做围栏的，你知道，所以我有很多管子和一台焊机。

sentences.en: So just went back there in the shop and welded some pipe together.
sentences.zh: 所以我就回到车间，把一些管子焊在一起。

sentences.en: Brad fashioned together a ladder that unfolded to a specific height, length, and width.
sentences.zh: 布拉德拼凑了一个可以展开到特定高度、长度和宽度的梯子。

sentences.en: The dimensions allowed it to go right over the T-posts and across the corner, all without ever touching the ranch's property.
sentences.zh: 这些尺寸使它能够直接越过T型柱并跨过角落，全程都没有触碰到牧场的财产。

sentences.en: And when the hunters crossed using Brad's ladder, just like the time before, other than those T-posts, there were no fences, no gates, no other infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 当猎人们使用布拉德的梯子穿越时，就像上次一样，除了那些T型柱，没有围栏，没有大门，也没有其他基础设施。

sentences.en: The hunters designed, built, set up, and climbed a specialized ladder to cross through empty airspace in an empty field.
sentences.zh: 猎人们设计、建造、架设并爬上了一个专门的梯子，穿过空旷田野上的空旷领空。

sentences.en: Just so they could say that, this time, they were following the very letter of the law.
sentences.zh: 只是为了让他们能说，这一次，他们是在严格遵守法律条文。

sentences.en: Hi, this is Stephen Grindy with Elk Mountain Ranch again, Colin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，科林，我是麋鹿山牧场的斯蒂芬·格林迪。

sentences.en: We had an issue with some truSt...
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了一些信任问题……

sentences.en: Not too long after the hunters got there, that same ranch manager from earlier, Steve Grindy, recognized their truck from the previous year.
sentences.zh: 猎人们到达后不久，之前提到的那位牧场经理史蒂夫·格林迪就认出了他们去年的那辆卡车。

sentences.en: He called local law enforcement agencies repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 他反复致电当地执法机构。

sentences.en: Eventually, a sheriff's deputy and fish and game officer both showed up.
sentences.zh: 最终，一名警长副手和一名鱼类与野生动物官员都赶到了现场。

sentences.en: How's it going?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Chris.
sentences.zh: 克里斯。

sentences.en: Steve.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫。

sentences.en: Here's the body cam footage.
sentences.zh: 这是随身摄像机的录像。

sentences.en: Have you seen them cornered back?
sentences.zh: 你看到他们从角落跨越了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we just watched them.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们刚看着他们。

sentences.en: I just watched them.
sentences.zh: 我刚看着他们。

sentences.en: And it's posted.
sentences.zh: 而且那里有告示。

sentences.en: I have signs right there, too.
sentences.zh: 我那里也有标志。

sentences.en: Jump this corner right here.
sentences.zh: 跳过这个角落。

sentences.en: What they have is a ladder that they put down and go over.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个梯子，他们把它放下来，然后跨过去。

sentences.en: Grindy's efforts to keep the hunters out of the public land went beyond phone calls to police.
sentences.zh: 格林迪为了阻止猎人进入公共土地所做的努力，不仅仅是给警察打电话。

sentences.en: At one point during the trip, Grindy poked his head in the hunter's tent and got escorted away by an officer.
sentences.zh: 在旅行期间，格林迪曾一度把头探进猎人的帐篷，被一名警官带走了。

sentences.en: Another time, he tracked the hunters down in his truck, cursed them out, and tailed them while they were hiking on a road that passes through public land.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，他开着卡车追踪猎人，咒骂他们，并在他们徒步经过一条穿过公共土地的道路时尾随他们。

sentences.en: And as the law enforcement officers giggled about the ladder in that body cam footage, a frustrated Grindy let this slip.
sentences.zh: 当执法人员在随身摄像机录像中对梯子咯咯笑时，沮丧的格林迪说漏了嘴。

sentences.en: Do they realize how much money my boss has?
sentences.zh: 他们知道我老板有多少钱吗？

sentences.en: The ranch was owned by a pharmaceutical executive from North Carolina named Fred Eshelman.
sentences.zh: 该牧场由一位名叫弗雷德·埃舍尔曼的北卡罗来纳州制药业高管拥有。

sentences.en: I reached out to Eshelman and his lawyers for an interview.
sentences.zh: 我联系了埃舍尔曼和他的律师寻求采访。

sentences.en: Neither got back to me.
sentences.zh: 两人都没有回复我。

sentences.en: But we know Eshelman told the ranch manager to keep talking to the authorities until they could get the hunters prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道埃舍尔曼告诉牧场经理继续与当局沟通，直到他们能起诉这些猎人。

sentences.en: And eventually, Eshelman's strategy worked.
sentences.zh: 最终，埃舍尔曼的策略奏效了。

sentences.en: The county attorney charged Brad, Phil, and their hunting partners, John Slewinski and Zachary Smith, with criminal trespass and sent a sheriff's deputy to their campsite.
sentences.zh: 县检察官指控布拉德、菲尔以及他们的狩猎伙伴约翰·斯莱温斯基和扎卡里·史密斯犯有刑事非法入侵罪，并派了一名警长副手到他们的营地。

sentences.en: Again, here's the body cam footage.
sentences.zh: 再次重申，这是随身摄像机的录像。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So just so it's not a surprise, you guys are all going to get cited for criminal trespass.
sentences.zh: 为了不让你们感到意外，你们所有人都要被传讯，罪名是刑事非法入侵。

sentences.en: But we still don't understand why.
sentences.zh: 但我们还是不明白为什么。

sentences.en: With this citation, the hunters were facing up to six months in jail, plus a big fine.
sentences.zh: 收到这张传票，猎人们面临最高六个月的监禁，外加巨额罚款。

sentences.en: So in Wyoming, it's if you go past a private boundary or a marked area, it is considered trespass.
sentences.zh: 在怀俄明州，如果你越过私人边界或标记区域，就被视为非法入侵。

sentences.en: So Elk Mountain Ranch is marked, is no trespassing.
sentences.zh: 所以麋鹿山牧场有标记，禁止非法入侵。

sentences.en: So that's what they're going to use is you guys went beyond the boundaries of the Elk Mountain Ranch.
sentences.zh: 所以他们要用的理由就是你们越过了麋鹿山牧场的边界。

sentences.en: But if I never touch Elk Mountain Ranch, you know, if I never touch the ranch, how did I trespass?
sentences.zh: 但如果我从未触碰麋鹿山牧场，你知道，如果我从未触碰过牧场，我怎么会非法入侵呢？

sentences.en: So this has been a point of contention in Wyoming for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这在怀俄明州长期以来一直是一个争论点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So especially so 20 miles north and south of the railroad is the checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 所以特别是铁路南北20英里处就是棋盘地带。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's been this way for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经持续很长时间了。

sentences.en: So hopefully you guys can come back and fight it.
sentences.zh: 所以希望你们能回来抗争。

sentences.en: When we come back, Brad and the other hunters do just that.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，布拉德和其他猎人正是这样做的。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注我们。

sentences.en: And we're back with the story of America's public lands and whose checkerboard it really is.
sentences.zh: 我们回来了，继续讲述美国公共土地的故事，以及这到底是谁的棋盘。

sentences.en: When the Wyoming Sheriff's Office charged the hunters with criminal trespassing on Fred Eshelman's land, things might very easily have just ended there.
sentences.zh: 当怀俄明州警长办公室指控猎人在弗雷德·埃舍尔曼的土地上进行刑事非法入侵时，事情本可以很容易地就此结束。

sentences.en: After all, at that point, it really was just a matter of corner crossing in this one area on this one ranch.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，在那一点上，这确实只是关于这个牧场这一特定区域的“角落穿越”问题。

sentences.en: There were plenty of other places in the country they could go hunt elk.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家，他们可以去打猎麋鹿的地方多的是。

sentences.en: You know, we went back and forth contemplating whether we were going to just plead guilty, pay the $750 or what it might be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们反复权衡过，到底是直接认罪，交那750美元罚款，还是怎么着。

sentences.en: None of us were too concerned about the six-month-in-jail type thing.
sentences.zh: 我们谁都没太把那六个月的监禁当回事。

sentences.en: But although the stakes for Brad and Phil and the other hunters personally were low, the principle involved seemed like part of something bigger,
sentences.zh: 但尽管布拉德、菲尔和其他猎人个人面临的风险很小，但其中涉及的原则问题似乎意义重大，

sentences.en: starting with their belief that corner crossing to access public land, which, again, is something hunters and other people do all the time, is legal.
sentences.zh: 首先是他们坚信，为了进入公共土地而进行“角落穿越”——再说一次，这是猎人和其他人一直在做的事情——是合法的。

sentences.en: It's such a simple concept.
sentences.zh: 这概念太简单了。

sentences.en: I got a six-year-old grandson.
sentences.zh: 我有个六岁的孙子。

sentences.en: I could point this to him very simply, and he would easily end up on the right side of this.
sentences.zh: 我可以很简单地指给他看，他会很容易地站在正确的一边。

sentences.en: This is just smoke and mirrors to try and steal the public's land.
sentences.zh: 这不过是试图窃取公共土地的烟雾弹和障眼法。

sentences.en: So they decided to lawyer up.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决定请律师。

sentences.en: To win, they would need someone with experience representing both hunters and ranchers.
sentences.zh: 为了胜诉，他们需要一个既有代表猎人经验，又有代表牧场主经验的人。

sentences.en: Someone who knew the laws, both spoken and unspoken, of the Mountain WeSt.
sentences.zh: 一个了解美国西部那些明文和不成文法律的人。

sentences.en: Someone who knew the difference between a mock scrape and a rub line.
sentences.zh: 一个能分清“模拟刮痕”和“磨擦线”区别的人。

sentences.en: They needed, when it came down to it, a guy like them.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，他们需要一个像他们一样的人。

sentences.en: They got Ryan.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了瑞安。

sentences.en: My name is Ryan Semerad.
sentences.zh: 我叫瑞安·塞梅拉德。

sentences.en: I am an attorney in Casper.
sentences.zh: 我是卡斯珀的一名律师。

sentences.en: Were you in tune with, I mean, were you a hunter, an angler?
sentences.zh: 你当时了解吗？我是说，你是个猎人或垂钓者吗？

sentences.en: Were you in tune with sort of public land issues in this case?
sentences.zh: 你当时关注这类公共土地问题吗？

sentences.en: No, I have never hunted.
sentences.zh: 不，我从没打过猎。

sentences.en: I think I have caught a fish once.
sentences.zh: 我想我只钓过一次鱼。

sentences.en: Ryan is originally from New York, not Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 瑞安来自纽约，而不是怀俄明州。

sentences.en: But his wife is from the area.
sentences.zh: 但他妻子是本地人。

sentences.en: And when they wanted to have kids, they decided to move closer to her family.
sentences.zh: 当他们想要孩子时，他们决定搬到离她家人更近的地方。

sentences.en: And that's what brought us back to Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 这就是把我们带回怀俄明州的原因。

sentences.en: And that is the only reason that I am here.
sentences.zh: 这也是我出现在这里的唯一原因。

sentences.en: At first, Ryan had no idea what to make of the case.
sentences.zh: 起初，瑞安根本不知道该怎么处理这个案子。

sentences.en: They described it as a corner hopping case.
sentences.zh: 他们把它描述为一起“角落穿越”案。

sentences.en: I assumed, and I was wrong, but I assumed that must have meant something really weird and rural,
sentences.zh: 我以为——虽然我错了，但我以为那一定是指某种非常奇怪的乡村琐事，

sentences.en: like a cow tipping case or something.
sentences.zh: 比如推牛案之类的。

sentences.en: Or you, you know, left your neighbor's gate open.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，没关好邻居的栅栏门。

sentences.en: But Ryan talked to some local friends.
sentences.zh: 但瑞安和一些当地朋友聊了聊。

sentences.en: They told him, this is a big deal here.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉他，这在当地可是件大事。

sentences.en: And it has been for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且已经持续很久了。

sentences.en: They sent him a study.
sentences.zh: 他们发给他一份研究报告。

sentences.en: And he learned that although a lot of the original checkerboarded area had been bought up and consolidated into these single land holdings,
sentences.zh: 他了解到，尽管最初许多棋盘状分布的土地已经被买下并整合成了单一的地产，

sentences.en: today, more than 8 million acres of public land across the western U.S.
sentences.zh: 但今天，美国西部仍有超过800万英亩的公共土地

sentences.en: remain corner locked.
sentences.zh: 处于“角落锁定”状态。

sentences.en: That's an area of public land only slightly smaller than Switzerland, completely inaccessible to anyone except for landowners like Eshelman.
sentences.zh: 那是一片仅比瑞士略小的公共土地，除了像埃舍尔曼这样的土地所有者外，其他人完全无法进入。

sentences.en: That's when it kind of dawned on me that this was maybe a bigger issue than just this one case.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我突然意识到，这可能不仅仅是这一个案子的问题，而是更大的议题。

sentences.en: So Ryan agreed to represent one of the hunters in the criminal trial.
sentences.zh: 于是瑞安同意在刑事审判中为其中一名猎人辩护。

sentences.en: But he ended up representing all of them in civil court when he got noticed that Fred Eshelman, the owner of the ranch, had decided to sue the hunters too.
sentences.zh: 但当他收到通知说牧场主弗雷德·埃舍尔曼也决定起诉这些猎人时，他最终在民事法庭上为他们所有人进行了辩护。

sentences.en: Eshelman argued that he had bought the ranch with an understanding that corner crossing was illegal.
sentences.zh: 埃舍尔曼辩称，他买下牧场时，认定“角落穿越”是非法的。

sentences.en: Suddenly allowing it now would mean an influx of hunters and recreationists regularly trespassing on his private property.
sentences.zh: 现在突然允许这种行为，意味着猎人和休闲爱好者会经常闯入他的私有财产。

sentences.en: The chaos, as he saw it, would effectively devalue the land.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，这种混乱会有效地导致土地贬值。

sentences.en: The exact dollar amount he was suing for changed over time.
sentences.zh: 他起诉的具体金额随着时间推移而变化。

sentences.en: But he put the total cost as high as $9 million.
sentences.zh: 但他提出的总额高达900万美元。

sentences.en: What is the reaction you're hearing from Phil and Brad and the others when they hear that?
sentences.zh: 当菲尔、布拉德和其他人听到这个数字时，他们的反应是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I will tell you, that was a pretty tough moment when you tell anybody, hey, you know, you have this exposure.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，我告诉你，当你告诉任何人“嘿，你知道吗，你面临这种风险”时，那是一个相当艰难的时刻。

sentences.en: And especially these guys.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对这些人来说。

sentences.en: I mean, these are not pharmaceutical executives.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们不是制药公司的高管。

sentences.en: They are not billionaires.
sentences.zh: 他们也不是亿万富翁。

sentences.en: $9 million, you know, that's financial apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 900万美元，你知道，那是金融末日。

sentences.en: Although, for two people facing financial apocalypse, Brad and Phil seemed pretty stoic about it.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，对于两个面临金融末日的人来说，布拉德和菲尔对此表现得相当淡定。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, I told you, I'm a truck mechanic.
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以我跟你说了，我是个卡车修理工。

sentences.en: Like, buddy, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 老兄，我不知道。

sentences.en: I guess my biggest concern was, you know, I want to make sure my wife, we still have a home.
sentences.zh: 我想我最大的担心是，你知道，我想确保我和我妻子还能有个家。

sentences.en: But I guess if he wants my 2013 Silverado, I guess he can take it.
sentences.zh: 但我想如果他想要我那辆2013年的雪佛兰索罗德，那他就拿去吧。

sentences.en: If anything, Eshelman had sued them for too much money for it to have the desired effect.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么的话，那就是埃舍尔曼起诉的金额太高了，反而达不到预期的效果。

sentences.en: Phil thought $9 million was laughable.
sentences.zh: 菲尔觉得900万美元简直可笑。

sentences.en: Brad, too.
sentences.zh: 布拉德也这么认为。

sentences.en: That dollar amount was so outrageous.
sentences.zh: 那个金额太离谱了。

sentences.en: If he would have said a couple hundred thousand, that would have scared me.
sentences.zh: 如果他要个几十万，那确实会吓到我。

sentences.en: But in the millions, you know, it just wasn't a realistic number.
sentences.zh: 但达到数百万，你知道，那根本不是一个现实的数字。

sentences.en: But Eshelman wasn't deterred.
sentences.zh: 但埃舍尔曼并没有被吓退。

sentences.en: He just kept applying more pressure.
sentences.zh: 他只是不断施加更大的压力。

sentences.en: I've never seen this happen before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未见过这种情况。

sentences.en: It kind of shocks me.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: While we were waiting for that criminal trial to begin, for the jury selection to begin, jurors are filing in, court staff are filing in.
sentences.zh: 就在我们等待刑事审判开始、等待陪审团遴选开始时，陪审员们正在入场，法院工作人员也在入场。

sentences.en: My guys are all sitting there.
sentences.zh: 我的当事人们都坐在那儿。

sentences.en: And a sheriff's deputy walks up to each of them and issues them one more citation in front of the jury.
sentences.zh: 然后一名治安官副手走到他们每个人面前，在陪审团面前又给他们开了一张传票。

sentences.en: So another ticket, another criminal charge, this time for that first crossing back in 2020, a whole year before the ordeal they thought they were being tried for.
sentences.zh: 所以又是一张罚单，又是一项刑事指控，这次是针对2020年的那次穿越，整整比他们以为自己受审的那次早了一年。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's that's when we first learned about that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那就是我们第一次得知这件事的时候。

sentences.en: And I kind of handed it to I kind of looked at Ryan.
sentences.zh: 我当时把它递给……我看了看瑞安。

sentences.en: I said, well, what do you want?
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你想要什么？

sentences.en: What do I do with this?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么处理这个？

sentences.en: He said, throw it in the trash.
sentences.zh: 他说，扔进垃圾桶。

sentences.en: And that's how the trial began.
sentences.zh: 审判就是这样开始的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好了。

sentences.en: Court's back in session.
sentences.zh: 法庭恢复开庭。

sentences.en: The matter before the court is the state of Wyoming versus Bradley Cape, John Slowinski, Philip Yeoman, and Zachary Smith.
sentences.zh: 法庭审理的案件是怀俄明州诉布拉德利·凯普、约翰·斯洛温斯基、菲利普·约曼和扎卡里·史密斯案。

sentences.en: In the criminal trial,
sentences.zh: 在刑事审判中，

sentences.en: the state's lawyers argued that even if the hunters didn't set foot on private land when they ballerinaed over the T-posts in 2020 or climbed over them in 2021,
sentences.zh: 州政府律师辩称，即使猎人在2020年跨越T型柱或2021年翻越它们时没有踏上私有土地，

sentences.en: they passed through air itself that's owned by the ranch.
sentences.zh: 他们也穿过了属于牧场的空气本身。

sentences.en: Being a property owner has value.
sentences.zh: 作为业主是有价值的。

sentences.en: It matters.
sentences.zh: 这很重要。

sentences.en: So do boundaries.
sentences.zh: 边界也很重要。

sentences.en: And in Wyoming, the law is you don't just own the ground.
sentences.zh: 在怀俄明州，法律规定你拥有的不仅仅是地面。

sentences.en: You don't own the earth.
sentences.zh: 你拥有的不仅仅是土地。

sentences.en: You own the airspace.
sentences.zh: 你还拥有领空。

sentences.en: How many of you knew that before you came here?
sentences.zh: 在来到这里之前，你们中有多少人知道这一点？

sentences.en: Ryan's defense consisted of a few different points.
sentences.zh: 瑞安的辩护由几个不同的要点组成。

sentences.en: But basically, it came down to this idea that the hunters never physically trespassed.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，归结为猎人从未进行物理入侵这一观点。

sentences.en: Plus, they had air and land rights, too.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们也有空气和土地权利。

sentences.en: Only in their case, it was the right of access to public land.
sentences.zh: 只不过在他们的案例中，这是进入公共土地的权利。

sentences.en: Government can't take away your land without compensating.
sentences.zh: 政府不能在没有补偿的情况下拿走你的土地。

sentences.en: That's a take.
sentences.zh: 那叫征收。

sentences.en: But just so, private landowners can't take the public land.
sentences.zh: 同样，私人土地所有者也不能拿走公共土地。

sentences.en: It's not theirs.
sentences.zh: 那不是他们的。

sentences.en: It's all of ours.
sentences.zh: 那是我们所有人的。

sentences.en: And as the trial wore on, something else was happening.
sentences.zh: 随着审判的进行，其他事情也在发生。

sentences.en: All sorts of other people started to take notice, including hunters and environmentalists who have been struggling with checkerboard enclosures for years.
sentences.zh: 各种各样的人开始注意到这一点，包括多年来一直与棋盘状土地围栏作斗争的猎人和环保主义者。

sentences.en: But also, hikers, bicyclists, and fishermen who, thanks to new GPS mapping apps, could now see the full extent of the checkerboard and all that inaccessible public land.
sentences.zh: 还有徒步旅行者、骑自行车的人和渔民，多亏了新的GPS地图应用程序，他们现在可以看到棋盘状土地的全貌以及所有那些无法进入的公共土地。

sentences.en: Journalists got interested, too.
sentences.zh: 记者们也产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: Even before the trials had ended, the New York Times, the Washington Post, and the Wall Street Journal all ran features about the four hunters from Missouri, their little ladder,
sentences.zh: 甚至在审判结束前，《纽约时报》、《华盛顿邮报》和《华尔街日报》都刊登了关于这四名来自密苏里州的猎人、他们的小梯子

sentences.en: and corner crossings.
sentences.zh: 以及“角落穿越”的专题报道。

sentences.en: Hunting and public lands advocacy groups rallied members, raising money for the defense.
sentences.zh: 狩猎和公共土地倡导组织召集成员，为辩护筹集资金。

sentences.en: And for those paying attention, the case became about something larger than just this one little square in Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 对于那些关注的人来说，这个案子已经不仅仅是怀俄明州这一个小方块的问题了。

sentences.en: It was about public access to public land all over the country.
sentences.zh: 它关乎全国范围内对公共土地的公共访问权。

sentences.en: The significance of it, the millions of acres, you know, the corner locked land, it just, it's public land.
sentences.zh: 它的意义，那数百万英亩，你知道，那些被“角落锁定”的土地，它就是公共土地。

sentences.en: That's what it is.
sentences.zh: 事实就是这样。

sentences.en: It belongs, it belongs to the public.
sentences.zh: 它属于，它属于公众。

sentences.en: Yeah, it belongs to everybody.
sentences.zh: 是的，它属于每个人。

sentences.en: And it shouldn't be monopolized.
sentences.zh: 它不应该被垄断。

sentences.en: I live in Montana, where there's a lot of public land, and also lots of checkerboarded country.
sentences.zh: 我住在蒙大拿州，那里有很多公共土地，也有很多棋盘状分布的乡村。

sentences.en: Even here, more than 500 miles from where Brad and Phil crossed, their case made waves.
sentences.zh: 即使在这里，距离布拉德和菲尔穿越的地方500多英里，他们的案子也引起了轰动。

sentences.en: I ran into a guy in a yoga class not too long ago wearing a corner crossing is not a crime t-shirt.
sentences.zh: 不久前，我在瑜伽课上遇到一个人，穿着一件写着“角落穿越不是犯罪”的T恤。

sentences.en: So, you get to a point where you can't back out.
sentences.zh: 所以，你到了一个无法退缩的地步。

sentences.en: It's a moral thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个道德问题。

sentences.en: It's all of that, right?
sentences.zh: 就是这一切，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's why it became bigger than us.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它变得比我们自身更重要。

sentences.en: And while the social status of the case got bigger, the legal stakes climbed too.
sentences.zh: 当案件的社会地位提升时，法律风险也随之攀升。

sentences.en: The Hunters won at both trials, but the civil case ended up before the U.S.
sentences.zh: 猎人们在两次审判中都赢了，但民事案件最终上诉到了美国

sentences.en: 10th Circuit Court of Appeals.
sentences.zh: 第十巡回上诉法院。

sentences.en: The 10th Circuit is based in Denver and oversees six western states.
sentences.zh: 第十巡回法院位于丹佛，管辖六个西部州。

sentences.en: This wasn't a small one-off case any longer, or even a case just setting the precedent in Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 这不再是一个小型的孤立案件，甚至不仅仅是一个在怀俄明州确立先例的案件。

sentences.en: The circuit court had the power to settle whether corner crossing was legal in all six of those states.
sentences.zh: 巡回法院有权决定“角落穿越”在那六个州是否合法。

sentences.en: The outcome would decide who got effective access to a huge amount of public land.
sentences.zh: 结果将决定谁能有效进入大量的公共土地。

sentences.en: And it was Eshelman's side, now backed up by a bunch of other landowners, that had appealed to the 10th Circuit.
sentences.zh: 正是埃舍尔曼一方，在其他一群土地所有者的支持下，向第十巡回法院提起了上诉。

sentences.en: They were the ones who wanted to go big.
sentences.zh: 他们才是想把事情闹大的人。

sentences.en: Ryan told me what he thought that meant.
sentences.zh: 瑞安告诉我他认为这意味着什么。

sentences.en: They have this kind of imperial intent that it's our lands, the lands they bought, and all of these public lands, too.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种帝国式的意图，认为这是我们的土地，他们买下的土地，以及所有这些公共土地，也都是他们的。

sentences.en: That's really what this case is about.
sentences.zh: 这才是这个案子的真正核心。

sentences.en: They're going to shut out the public from the public lands.
sentences.zh: 他们要将公众拒之于公共土地之外。

sentences.en: So May 2024, you're in Denver.
sentences.zh: 所以2024年5月，你在丹佛。

sentences.en: Have you made arguments in front of a circuit court before?
sentences.zh: 你以前在巡回法院进行过辩论吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Their very first time.
sentences.zh: 这是他们第一次。

sentences.en: Looks like everybody's ready to go.
sentences.zh: 看起来大家都准备好了。

sentences.en: With that, let's call the first case.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们传唤第一个案件。

sentences.en: Which is 23-8043 Iron Bar Holdings versus Cape, you may proceed.
sentences.zh: 即23-8043号，铁吧控股诉凯普案，你们可以开始了。

sentences.en: Good morning, Your Honors.
sentences.zh: 早上好，法官阁下。

sentences.en: May it please be court.
sentences.zh: 请允许法庭开庭。

sentences.en: The morning of the 10th Circuit hearing, an armada of well-respected attorneys showed up representing Eshelman.
sentences.zh: 第十巡回法院听证会那天早上，一群受人尊敬的律师代表埃舍尔曼出庭。

sentences.en: And since Eshelman's side brought the suit, they went firSt.
sentences.zh: 由于是埃舍尔曼一方提起的诉讼，他们先发言。

sentences.en: Some of the arguments had more or less stayed the same from the criminal trial.
sentences.zh: 一些论点在刑事审判后几乎没有改变。

sentences.en: But now things got more nuanced.
sentences.zh: 但现在情况变得更加微妙了。

sentences.en: First, Eshelman's team argued that private property is a building block of society.
sentences.zh: 首先，埃舍尔曼的团队辩称，私有财产是社会的基石。

sentences.en: Property lines have sharp edges because of the consequences of eroding them.
sentences.zh: 由于侵蚀财产边界会带来后果，所以财产界线必须清晰明确。

sentences.en: So there's practical implications of this case that I want to address.
sentences.zh: 所以这个案子有我想解决的实际影响。

sentences.en: The gist of their argument was what Eshelman had maintained all along, that whatever high ideals we might have about public lands,
sentences.zh: 他们论点的核心正如埃舍尔曼一直坚持的那样，无论我们对公共土地抱有何种崇高的理想，

sentences.en: the on-the-ground reality was that legalizing corner crossing would be an invitation for chaos.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，将“对角跨越”合法化只会招致混乱。

sentences.en: In places without government survey markers, and there often aren't any, people would start to accidentally trespass all the time if corner crossing was legalized.
sentences.zh: 在没有政府测量标记的地方——而且往往确实没有——如果将对角跨越合法化，人们就会开始不断地发生意外越界。

sentences.en: But also, there was no need to permit corner crossing.
sentences.zh: 而且，也没有必要允许对角跨越。

sentences.en: The government already had better tools at its disposal to resolve the problems created by the checkerboard.
sentences.zh: 政府已经有更好的工具来解决棋盘式土地布局所带来的问题。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, if the government wants to create access, just as they have gone from 150 million acres of originally locked land, today less than 9 million remains.
sentences.zh: 如果政府明天想要创造通行权，就像他们当初将原本被锁定的1.5亿英亩土地减少到今天不足900万英亩一样，

sentences.en: They are making progress.
sentences.zh: 他们正在取得进展。

sentences.en: And that's true.
sentences.zh: 事实确实如此。

sentences.en: Although those last 9 million acres have proven tricky to eradicate,
sentences.zh: 尽管最后这900万英亩土地已被证明难以消除，

sentences.en: there are various mechanisms for erasing the private squares in the checkerboard or just letting the public pass through.
sentences.zh: 但仍有各种机制可以抹去棋盘中的私人方块，或者仅仅是让公众通过。

sentences.en: Eshelman's side argued there's no need to override all that policy for the sake of some elk-hungry hunters.
sentences.zh: 埃舍尔曼一方认为，没有必要为了满足一些渴望猎鹿的猎人而推翻所有这些政策。

sentences.en: If anything, this is a question for the legislature and local agencies, not the courts.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，这应该是立法机构和地方机构的问题，而不是法院的问题。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Brad and Phil and the other hunters were streaming the proceedings from Missouri.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，布拉德、菲尔和其他猎人在密苏里州通过流媒体观看了庭审过程。

sentences.en: They didn't attend the oral arguments in person.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有亲自参加口头辩论。

sentences.en: When you watched it, did you guys get together?
sentences.zh: 你们看的时候聚在一起了吗？

sentences.en: Did you watch it separately?
sentences.zh: 还是分开看的？

sentences.en: No, we watched it separately.
sentences.zh: 不，我们是分开看的。

sentences.en: We all work.
sentences.zh: 我们都要工作。

sentences.en: May it please the court.
sentences.zh: 请求法庭准许。

sentences.en: Ryan Sumner after the F-A-L-E-S.
sentences.zh: 我是瑞安·萨姆纳，代表费尔斯一方。

sentences.en: When it was Ryan's turn to speak, Brad and Phil could both tell as they listened in that Ryan's core arguments were also much the same as in that first trial.
sentences.zh: 当轮到瑞安发言时，布拉德和菲尔在监听时都能听出，瑞安的核心论点与第一次审判时基本相同。

sentences.en: You can't exploit the interlocking land pattern to deny everybody else the benefits while you reap them all.
sentences.zh: 你不能利用这种交错的土地格局来剥夺其他所有人的利益，而自己却独享这一切。

sentences.en: But this one moment toward the end of the hearing stood out to them both.
sentences.zh: 但听证会临近结束时的一个瞬间，给他们两人留下了深刻印象。

sentences.en: For me, it was when, and I don't remember the judge's name, he said, yeah, I don't believe our Congress intended,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是当——我不记得法官的名字了——他说，是的，我不相信我们的国会，

sentences.en: when they wrote the laws and this checkerboard pattern was first made, they didn't intend it to block the public.
sentences.zh: 在制定法律和最初形成这种棋盘式格局时，他们的本意是阻挡公众。

sentences.en: If you look back at when the railroads were going across, Congress said, we want to give the railroads half the land and the public half the land.
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾铁路建设时期，国会说，我们想把一半土地给铁路公司，另一半给公众。

sentences.en: Did Congress really intend, the judge asked, for the public to have no real right to the land from their half of the deal?
sentences.zh: 法官问道，国会真的打算让公众在他们那份交易中对土地没有任何真正的权利吗？

sentences.en: If somebody had just posed the question that way to Congress, I have no doubt how they would have answered that question.
sentences.zh: 如果当时有人向国会提出这个问题，我毫不怀疑他们会如何回答。

sentences.en: This past March, nearly a year after the oral arguments in Denver, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今年三月，在丹佛口头辩论近一年后，美国

sentences.en: 10th Circuit Court of Appeals issued its opinion on the case of Iron Bar Holdings v.
sentences.zh: 第十巡回上诉法院就“铁吧控股诉凯普案”发布了裁决意见。

sentences.en: Cape.
sentences.zh: 凯普。

sentences.en: That day, Ryan was in court in Wyoming.
sentences.zh: 那天，瑞安正在怀俄明州的法庭上。

sentences.en: So I try to rush back to the office and I print off the opinion and I sit down to read it and just, what am I about to read?
sentences.zh: 所以我试着赶回办公室，打印出裁决书，坐下来阅读，心里想着，我到底要读到什么？

sentences.en: And as I read it, it was just, it was perfect.
sentences.zh: 当我读到它时，简直太完美了。

sentences.en: In many ways, the opinion was everything Ryan and Brad and the other hunters had argued for since the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这份裁决意见正是瑞安、布拉德和其他猎人从一开始就一直主张的。

sentences.en: The court laid out the history of the West, the railroads, the checkerboard grants, the enclosures, the range wars.
sentences.zh: 法院梳理了西部的历史、铁路、棋盘式土地赠与、圈地运动以及牧场战争。

sentences.en: It explained how the land is supposed to work.
sentences.zh: 它解释了土地应该如何运作。

sentences.en: The opinion said, these public lands in the West, they're for everyone, and that's who they were always for.
sentences.zh: 裁决意见称，西部这些公共土地是属于每个人的，它们一直以来就是为所有人准备的。

sentences.en: So, we win.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们赢了。

sentences.en: Corner Crossing is not a trespass in all six states.
sentences.zh: 在所有六个州，对角跨越都不再构成非法入侵。

sentences.en: The 10th Circuit's decision won't bring total closure.
sentences.zh: 第十巡回法院的裁决并不会带来彻底的终结。

sentences.en: After Eshelman's team appealed again, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在埃舍尔曼团队再次上诉后，美国

sentences.en: Supreme Court refused to take up the case.
sentences.zh: 最高法院拒绝受理此案。

sentences.en: Which means that, for now at least, the status of corner crossing and public land access in the other 44 states remains murky.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，至少目前为止，对角跨越和公共土地准入在其他44个州的状态依然模糊不清。

sentences.en: The last time I met up with Brad and Phil, they are passing through where I live, on their way to their big annual Western hunting trip, this time in Montana.
sentences.zh: 我最后一次见到布拉德和菲尔时，他们正路过我住的地方，前往他们一年一度的西部大型狩猎之旅，这次是在蒙大拿州。

sentences.en: Here, we're in the 9th Circuit, along with other Western states with lots of checkerboarded land like Idaho, Oregon, and Washington.
sentences.zh: 这里属于第九巡回法院管辖区，和爱达荷州、俄勒冈州、华盛顿州等其他拥有大量棋盘式土地的西部州一样。

sentences.en: Montana's Fish and Game Agency has said, corner crossing remains unlawful here, so don't do it.
sentences.zh: 蒙大拿州的鱼类和野生动物管理局表示，在这里对角跨越仍然是非法的，所以不要这样做。

sentences.en: But other authorities in the state disagree, and the issue remains as unclear as ever.
sentences.zh: 但该州的其他当局对此持不同意见，这个问题依然像以往一样不明确。

sentences.en: It's unlikely Brad and Phil will be involved in whatever comes next.
sentences.zh: 布拉德和菲尔不太可能参与接下来的任何事情了。

sentences.en: The whole saga has already taken up four years of their lives, and that, they said, was enough.
sentences.zh: 整个事件已经占据了他们四年的生活，他们说，这已经足够了。

sentences.en: But talking with them, I could tell they're a little bit bummed the Supreme Court didn't take up the case.
sentences.zh: 但与他们交谈时，我能感觉到他们对最高法院没有受理此案感到有些沮丧。

sentences.en: The way they see it, there's still more locked up land that needs to be freed.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，还有更多被锁定的土地需要被解放。

sentences.en: You could never dream in a million years that you would end up here over something so simple as making one step.
sentences.zh: 你做梦也不会想到，仅仅因为迈出一步这样简单的事情，你最后会走到这一步。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, we didn't set out to do this.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你知道，我们并不是刻意要这么做。

sentences.en: But, you know, we just wanted to go hunt elk.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们只是想去猎鹿。

sentences.en: Would you guys ever corner cross again?
sentences.zh: 你们还会再进行对角跨越吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对会。

sentences.en: We put in now every year since, I believe, for Elk Mountain.
sentences.zh: 我相信从那以后，我们每年都为麋鹿山申请许可。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We're going back.
sentences.zh: 我们会回去的。

sentences.en: We don't know when, but we're going back.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道什么时候，但我们会回去的。

sentences.en: Why do you want to go back so bad?
sentences.zh: 为什么你们这么想回去？

sentences.en: I think because we can.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为我们可以。
